title: Query string parser (jQuery era, ES5)
criteria: THE parseQueryString function SHALL accept a query string with or without a leading question mark and SHALL return an object that maps decoded keys to decoded values.
WHEN the input is empty or contains only a question mark, THE parseQueryString function SHALL return an empty object.
WHEN a pair has no equals sign, THE parseQueryString function SHALL use the empty string as its value.
WHEN a key appears more than once, THE parseQueryString function SHALL return an array that holds every value in order of appearance.
WHEN a key or a value contains a plus sign, THE parseQueryString function SHALL decode it as a space before percent-decoding.
IF a percent-encoded sequence is malformed, THEN THE parseQueryString function SHALL throw a URIError.
WHERE a key is __proto__, THE parseQueryString function SHALL ignore the pair.
design:
# Design: Query string parser

Entry function: `parseQueryString(query)`.

Input: a string, the URL query part with or without a leading question mark.

Output: an object that maps each decoded key to a decoded string, or to an array of strings when the key repeats.

The function is pure and deterministic. The TypeScript version types the result as a record of strings or string arrays, uses `startsWith` and `Array.isArray` instead of loose comparisons, and skips the `__proto__` key explicitly.

invariants.input: string: a URL query string, with or without a leading question mark
invariants.output: object mapping string keys to a string or to an array of strings
list: Empty pairs created by consecutive ampersands are skipped.
The first occurrence of a key stores a string and later occurrences store an array of strings.
The key __proto__ never changes the prototype of the result and never appears as an own property.
A malformed percent-encoded sequence throws a URIError.
Calling the function twice with the same input returns deeply equal objects.

curses.description: Writes a property whose name comes from user input. Keys such as __proto__ or constructor reach inherited members of the result object.
curses.strategy: Skip dangerous keys explicitly, or store entries in a Map or in an object created with Object.create(null).

curses.description: The var declarations inside the loop are hoisted to function scope, so separator, rawKey, and rawValue leak out of each iteration.
curses.strategy: Declare the per-iteration values with const inside a for...of loop.

curses.description: Loose equality compares through implicit conversion, which hides type mistakes in the comparison.
curses.strategy: Use startsWith or strict equality so that only strings are compared.

curses.description: Detects arrays through a string comparison with loose equality instead of a direct type check.
curses.strategy: Replace the check with Array.isArray, which needs no string comparison.
